articles.title: Bill Maher Rubs Salt in Trump’s Midterms Wound: ‘Donnie, Are You OK?’
articles.summary: While his HBO counterpart John Oliver issued an urgent warning about voting GOP during the midterms, Bill Maher spent the majority of his time in the lead-up to the critical election dining with the Trump at the White House (and then bickering with him publicly), conducting an embarrassingly…
body: He wasn’t done. “Well, look, I hate to gloat, but sorry, I have to do a little bit because everybody was hedging about this election,” Maher said, before pointing to a series clips of himself on “Real Time” and various cable news programs predicting that the Democrats would deliver a “historical thumping” to the Republicans during the midterms.

“Here’s something I could not have predicted: Trump’s reaction to the election. He said, ‘Congratulations to the Democrats, they did a good job,’” offered Maher, before looking directly into the camera and addressing his sparring partner: “Donnie, are you OK? I know we’ve been feuding. You sound unwell. You’re not even going to fake it was rigged?”

articles.summary: As James Bond casting rumors heat up, a couple more A-list actors have entered the mix: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were among the stars who screen-tested to play the new 007.
body: Last year, Amazon MGM Studios tapped Villeneuve as the franchise’s next director, with “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight hired to write the script. Getting Bond 26 off the ground has been a top priority for the property’s new stewards, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman.

Since then, nearly every 30-something British actor’s name has been bandied about in the U.K. and U.S. press, with rumored top contenders including Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. Variety has learned that Harry Styles has had discussions about the part, and Theo James also hasn’t been ruled out.

articles.title: Chang Chen Urges Emerging Taiwanese Actors to ‘Be Like Water’ at Taiwan Creative Content Fest Golden Horse Showcase
articles.summary: Chang Chen, chair of the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee and last year’s Golden Horse best leading actor winner for “Lucky Lu,” advised six of Taiwan’s rising performers on working across different film sets at a Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) showcase in Taipei.
body: The lineup drew from two consecutive Golden Horse Awards cycles. Bai and Ho are nominees for this year’s Best New Performer award for “Girl” and “Sunshine Women’s Choir,” respectively. Ma won the award last year for “Left-Handed Girl,” while Rosen, Liu and Lin were nominated for “Marching Boys,” “Blind Love” and “A Dance With Rainbows,” respectively.

Bai, who began acting at 6, is now a university student studying film. She greeted the audience in Mandarin and Japanese and said she had trained in traditional Chinese martial arts for a decade. Ho, who described herself as slow to warm up, serious and full of contrasts, drew on her extensive dance training; she hopes to take on a suspense action film or other physically forceful roles.
Liu said he had practiced taekwondo for seven years. “At this stage, I feel it’s more important to light up others than to light up myself,” Lin said.

Ma said acting helps her find an outlet for pressure. “When you give yourself completely to a role, audiences can feel your sincerity,” she said. “It can give others strength and help you understand yourself better.”

articles.title: ‘Fire Country’ and ‘Sheriff Country’ Bosses Break Down the Crossover Episode, ‘Con Air’ Influences and the Potential Romance That Wasn’t on the Page
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for “Sheriff Country” Season 2, Episode 5, “No Way In” and “Fire Country” Season 5, Episode 5, “No Way Out.” Both series stream on Paramount+.
body: It was all hands on deck for the most recent crossover between CBS procedurals “Sheriff Country” and “Fire Country.” A raging wildfire sent Manny (Kevin Alejandro) and the rest of Station 42 to the Edgewater Police Department to ask Mickey (Morena Baccarin) and her squad for help evacuating residents if the flames moved closer to town. The request was made a bit awkward by the reveal that Manny and Mickey once went on a date from hell after being paired up at the police department’s annual date auction.

There wasn’t too much time to dwell on that, as the mission was complicated by the news of a prison break. Three women inmates escaped a transport van in the midst of the fire chaos, and Mickey needed her troops to find the missing convicts instead of helping with the fire. Mickey ultimately sacrificed herself to the convicts after they were found at The Meat Up, and would only let the hostages inside go if Mickey let them take her daughter, Skye (Amanda Arcuri), with them as collateral to make it across the county border.

articles.title: Sebastián Lelio was a fascinating film-maker of great passion and poetry
articles.summary: Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman could expertly capture both the personal and political. Sebastián Lelio, director of A Fantastic Woman and Gloria, dies aged 52. The last 20 years have seen an amazing flowering of creativity from Chilean film-makers.
body: But there can hardly be a director who dramatized the different aspects of Chile’s complex and conflicted 21st-century zeitgeist than Sebastián Lelio. Some of his films were political and some not obviously political. But they were all fierce, passionate and sensual – an expression of defiance, at some level, against a system which robbed ordinary people of pleasure.

Lelio’s 2017 film Disobedience, his English-language debut, starring Rachel Weisz and Rachel McAdams, was a London-set movie about a conservative Jewish community in which Weisz plays Ronit, a rabbi’s daughter whose secret gay identity flowers once her father is dead in circumstances of unbearable tension. It is a fascinating film, all the more intriguing perhaps in that it is happening outside Lelio’s Latin American heartland under gray British skies.
points: Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman could expertly capture both the personal and political.

articles.title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
articles.summary: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate. Over a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat.
body: Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless debuts in front of this movie.) Warner has one of the most storied animation libraries in American cinema (and, for that matter, plenty of great animated TV shows like Batman: The Animated Series and Animaniacs) but as far as features go, they’ve never settled on a clear creative vision. They seem just as adrift in a landscape crowded with serious competitors as they were back when everyone was imitating Disney.

When the Cat arrives, he eventually – the movie’s set-up, midsection and climax are all painfully distended – whisks the kids and their suddenly talking goldfish Waffles (Matt Berry, the other vocal MVP of the cast) into a series of magical lands expanded from the family’s possessions. They’re in search of the Cat’s Go-Backer device, which Gabby hopes to use to undo their family’s move, and pursued by a shadowy, gigantic creature called Something.

articles.title: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
articles.summary: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope not. A long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up…
body: It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.”

Pugh’s analogy becomes stranger the more you think about it. Lucas may have drawn heavily on Frank Herbert’s original 1965 book when he dreamed up the desert planet of Tatooine, but the two sagas offer distinctly different views of the universe. The original Star Wars trilogy asked us to believe that its central villain was ultimately worthy of redemption, despite having been a powerful cog in a regime responsible for billions of deaths. Dune, by contrast, is flowing grimly in exactly the opposite direction.
points: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera.

Disney did not disclose viewing figures. The global premiere record is based on views during the show’s first three days of availability.

The 2023 superhero drama became Disney+ and Hulu’s most watched Korean original and was a particularly powerful draw in South Korea and across Asia. articles.title: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom
articles.summary: She started acting at six and by 16 was starring in Even Stevens with Shia LaBeouf. Then her career fell apart. Here, she explains how she survived growing up in the spotlight. In a class at college, Christy Carlson Romano was encouraged to think about her “community”.
body: The title of her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck, gives you a flavour of where Carlson Romano, 42, is coming from, but what’s most striking isn’t that she goes off the rails (she doesn’t, hugely, compared to other former child stars), but how sensible and mature she is as a child. It’s alarming. When fans recognise her now – she was in the popular Disney series Even Stevens which started in 2000 – they tell her she was a huge part of their childhoods. She had been acting the part of a normal suburban girl, the perfectionist Ren Stevens, while having no idea what that was like. She was already a mini adult.

Now Carlson Romano has a social media career, which has given her a detachment from the entertainment industry. “I’m outspoken at this point, but for a lot of people they can’t do that,” she says. “What hurts is when I see other child actors suffering, because I know that means they haven’t found their way through the pain.” We speak, over Zoom, not long after Hayden Panettiere, the “Nashville” actor and singer who had started as a child and had talked about her experience of early fame, addiction and mental illness, had been found dead.

articles.title: Albert Brooks Predicted Ozempic. Now He’s Predicting President Ossoff
articles.summary: In his 2011 novel 'Twenty Thirty,' he imagined a blockbuster weight-loss drug, a generational war — and a Jewish president. "God damn it," he recently told a friend. "My entire book is going to come true.”
body: By the fifth sentence of Twenty Thirty, Albert Brooks already looks like a modern-day Nostradamus. At an 80th birthday party in the 2011 novel, everyone looks suspiciously good, due in part to “a new weight-loss drug” that “works almost 100 percent of the time, in everyone.”
Then come the computer watches, the self-driving vehicles and a generation of young people furious at their elders for living so long and consuming so much of the country’s wealth.

In the novel, a candidate named Matthew Bernstein, the son of a Jewish father and a non-Jewish mother, wins the 2028 election and becomes America’s first Jewish president. Brooks, 79, was watching Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff’s final campaign speech when he thought of Bernstein. Ossoff also has a Jewish father and a non-Jewish mother. Brooks called a close friend.
“God damn it,” he remembers saying. “My entire book is going to come true.”
points: In his 2011 novel 'Twenty Thirty,' he imagined a blockbuster weight-loss drug, a generational war — and a Jewish president.

articles.title: Justin Timberlake Teases New Music: “I’ve Been Chef-ing”
articles.summary: The Grammy- and Emmy-winning singer hints at fresh material he's worked on with Don Toliver, Quavo, Pharrell and Timbaland and explains why he was originally told hit "SexyBack" wasn't "gonna work."
body: It’s been a little over a year since Justin Timberlake wrapped his Forget Tomorrow world tour, promoting his sixth solo album Everything I Thought It Was, released in 2024, but he’s already cooking up something new.
The Grammy- and Emmy-winning singer said he’s “been working” in Miami and hinted at new music, particularly in the form of collaborations with Pharrell Williams, Quavo, Don Toliver and Timbaland.

In the video, where Timberlake revisited some of his most beloved songs, he spoke at length specifically about working with Toliver, explaining how his son played a role in his “easy decision” to clear a “Rock Your Body” sample for Toliver’s “Body.”

“As soon as I heard it, I was like, yeah, of course,” Timberlake said. “My 11-year-old, Silas, Don Toliver, that’s his guy, I remember asking him… and he was like, ‘You gotta do it.’ So that was an easy yes. I also really love that whole album.”
